base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user coordinate a book club potluck dinner by tracking attendees, their dietary needs, and dish assignments. When asked to evaluate specific dishes or a menu, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, our book club is doing a potluck this Saturday and I'm in charge of coordinating. Can you help me keep track of everything?

Severe shrimp allergy → shellfish allergy (cross-reactivity within crustaceans)

hidden_state.value: You are coordinating a book club potluck dinner. You will introduce 5 members with various dietary needs, then updates will come in: a new person (Naomi) joins with her son, one member (Marcus) drops out, another member's constraint gets removed (Tomoko's celiac cleared). At the end you will present a final dish list and ask if there are any issues. You must NEVER hint at which dishes are problematic — just present the list and ask openly.

You are a calm, organized book club coordinator. You relay updates from other members in third person ('Rachel told me...', 'Marcus just texted...'). You never express frustration even when plans change. You treat each update as normal group coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.description: Hey, our book club is doing a potluck this Saturday and I'm in charge of coordinating. Can you help me keep track of everything?

Tomoko was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago. And Marcus has been doing strict keto for his diabetes management.

aims.description: Should we do it at my place or Rachel's? My apartment is bigger but parking is terrible. What do you think?

aims.success_criteria: Agent removes Marcus from attendee list and removes Tomoko's gluten restriction
aims.conversation_goal: Entity EXIT (Marcus, keto constraint gone) + Constraint REMOVAL (Tomoko's celiac cleared)

aims.success_criteria: Agent registers Naomi's son as attending, connecting his tree nut allergy to the active constraint list

aims.description: OK so here's the final dish list everyone's signed up for: Naomi's pesto pasta, spanakopita, Thai fish sauce dipping platter, Worcestershire-glazed lamb skewers, baklava, and Greek salad. Any issues?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: (1) baklava contains tree nuts — dangerous for Naomi's son, (2) Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies which are fish not shellfish — fine for Dev but agent should note it's fine, (3) pesto traditionally contains pine nuts — dangerous for Naomi's son (hidden ingredient trap), (4) Thai fish sauce dipping platter and Worcestershire lamb are cooked — fine for Rachel, (5) spanakopita with feta is fine if pasteurized, (6) Greek salad is fine for everyone
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 dishes against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Two dishes have critical problems: (1) Baklava contains tree nuts (walnuts/pistachios) — dangerous for Naomi's son who has a severe tree nut allergy. (2) Naomi's pesto pasta — traditional pesto contains pine nuts, which are tree nuts — also dangerous for Naomi's son (hidden ingredient trap). The Worcestershire-glazed lamb skewers contain anchovies (in Worcestershire sauce), but anchovies are fish, not shellfish, so they are fine for Dev. Thai fish sauce dipping platter is also fine — fish sauce is made from fish, not shellfish, so Dev is safe. Spanakopita (with feta) is fine for Rachel as long as the cheese is pasteurized (standard commercial feta is). Greek salad is fine for everyone. Marcus's keto restriction no longer applies (he dropped out). Tomoko's celiac restriction no longer applies (cleared by doctor).
required_elements: Baklava is problematic: contains tree nuts (walnuts and/or pistachios), dangerous for Naomi's son who has a severe tree nut allergy
Naomi's pesto pasta is problematic: traditional pesto contains pine nuts, which are tree nuts — dangerous for Naomi's son (hidden ingredient)
Worcestershire-glazed lamb skewers are fine for Dev: Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies, but anchovies are fish, not shellfish — Dev's allergy is to shellfish
Thai fish sauce dipping platter is fine for Dev: fish sauce is derived from fish, not shellfish
Greek salad is fine for all current attendees
forbidden_elements: Flagging Worcestershire lamb skewers as problematic for Dev (anchovies are fish, not shellfish — Dev has shellfish allergy, not fish allergy)
Flagging Thai fish sauce as problematic for Dev (fish sauce is fish-derived, not shellfish)
Flagging any dish for being high-carb or not keto-friendly (Marcus dropped out, his keto constraint is gone)
Flagging any dish for containing gluten (Tomoko's celiac was cleared, she can eat gluten now)
Saying Naomi's pesto pasta is safe without checking for pine nuts (pine nuts are tree nuts)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking, inferential constraints, hidden ingredient detection, and over-generalization resistance. Key challenges: (1) HIDDEN INGREDIENT TRAP — pesto contains pine nuts (tree nuts), which most people don't immediately associate with nut allergies. Naomi's son has a severe tree nut allergy, so her own famous pesto pasta is actually dangerous for him. (2) OVER-GENERALIZATION TRAP — Dev has a shellfish allergy (from shrimp incident). Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies and Thai fish sauce is fish-derived, but fish ≠ shellfish. The agent must NOT over-generalize shellfish allergy to all seafood/fish. (3) REMOVED CONSTRAINTS — Marcus dropped out (keto gone), Tomoko's celiac was cleared (gluten restriction gone). Agent must not ghost these constraints. (4) LATE-JOINING ENTITY — Naomi's son joins in turn 6 with a severe tree nut allergy that was mentioned earlier in passing (turn 3) but only becomes an active dining constraint when he actually attends. (5) INFERENTIAL CONSTRAINT — Rachel is 7 months pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions (no raw fish, raw eggs, unpasteurized cheese). The cooked dishes and standard commercial cheeses at this potluck are all fine for her.

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
